panels.description: Webhook request count per adaptive time interval, by HTTP status.
panels.title: HTTP Requests

panels.description: Authentication failures by reason.
panels.title: Auth Failures

panels.description: Successfully published webhook messages per adaptive time interval.
panels.title: Messages Published

panels.description: End-to-end webhook request latency percentiles.
panels.title: Request Duration

panels.description: Requests rejected before publish (IP allowlist, replay, rate limit, saturation).
panels.title: Pre-publish Rejections

panels.description: Webhook deliveries dropped by endpoint or route filter chains, per adaptive time interval. level=endpoint drops the whole delivery; level=route skips a single destination.
panels.title: Filtered Deliveries

panels.description: Enabled endpoints and their routing targets from loaded config.
panels.title: Endpoints

panels.description: Configured RabbitMQ (or other) destinations from loaded config.
panels.title: Destinations

panels.description: RabbitMQ publish latency percentiles.
panels.title: Publish Duration

panels.description: Successful and failed publish attempts per adaptive time interval.
panels.title: Publish Attempts

panels.description: Webhook delivery attempts by outcome per adaptive time interval. Outcome 2xx is success; 4xx/5xx/429/timeout/error are failures. Delivery is async, so this — not the HTTP 202 accept — is the true signal of whether payloads reach the destination.
panels.title: Webhook Deliveries by Outcome

panels.description: Webhook delivery retries per adaptive time interval (a retry is any attempt after the first, triggered by 429/5xx/timeout). A rising rate means the destination is flaky or slow.
panels.title: Webhook Retries

panels.description: Webhook deliveries dropped because the async queue was full (backpressure). Any sustained non-zero value means the delivery workers cannot keep up — raise server.fanout_concurrency or the destination's max_queue.
panels.title: Webhook Dropped

panels.description: Process CPU usage (cores).
panels.title: CPU Usage

panels.description: Process resident memory and Go heap allocation.
panels.title: Memory

panels.description: Terminally-failed async webhook deliveries redirected to a dead-letter destination, by original failure outcome. Sustained volume means a webhook target is persistently failing.
panels.title: Webhook Dead-Letters

panels.description: The dead-letter redirect ITSELF failed — the event is lost. Any non-zero value is a data-loss incident; alert on it.
panels.title: Webhook Dead-Letter Failures (event lost)

panels.description: Per-destination async webhook queue depth against its configured capacity. Depth approaching capacity precedes drops (see Webhook Dropped).
panels.title: Webhook Queue Depth vs Capacity

panels.description: Mandatory RabbitMQ publishes the broker returned as unroutable (no bound queue) — the message is lost. Non-zero means a routing/binding misconfiguration.
panels.title: RabbitMQ Unroutable (lost)

panels.description: Messages published to a configured RabbitMQ dead-letter exchange. Informational; correlates with consumer-side rejections.
panels.title: RabbitMQ DLX Publishes

panels.description: Redis pub/sub publishes that reached zero subscribers (at-most-once discard). Non-zero means no consumer was listening when the event fired.
panels.title: Redis Pub/Sub Dropped (no subscriber)

panels.description: Recovered panics by where they were caught (handler, fanout, webhook_worker, readiness_prober, replay_cleanup). Any non-zero value warrants investigation.
panels.title: Panics by Location

panels.description: Per-destination readiness (1 ready / 0 not ready) as observed by the background readiness prober. A destination dropping to 0 is degraded; the store is non-gating so this is observability only.
panels.title: Destination Readiness

panels.description: Replay Postgres store reachability from the cleanup loop's Ping (1 up / 0 down). Best-effort and NON-gating: a down store never pulls the pod from rotation, but capture gaps accrue while down.
panels.title: Replay Store Up

panels.description: The running binary's version and commit (from -ldflags). Use to confirm a rollout reached this instance.
panels.title: Build Info

panels.description: Authenticated webhook events written to the replay store at ingest, by endpoint. The capture rate should track accepted HTTP requests for capture-enabled endpoints.
panels.title: Events Captured

panels.description: Best-effort replay-store write failures by op (insert = capture at ingest, update = per-destination outcome). These never affect the webhook response; sustained values mean a degraded store and replay-record gaps.
panels.title: Capture Failures

panels.description: Events replayed via the protected API, by mode (single / bulk). Each counts one event fanned out to its recorded destinations.
panels.title: Replays Triggered

panels.description: Replay events deleted by the cleanup loop (by age ttl and/or volume max_events). Zero with a growing store means neither bound is set.
panels.title: Events Purged

panels.description: Per-node execution latency (p50/p95/p99). Labels are config-bounded (flow, node_id, node_type) — never rendered lookup targets.
panels.title: Node Duration
